scope: Unnamed, process-local CreateEventA, SetEvent and ResetEvent integrated with the existing WaitForSingleObject, DuplicateHandle and CloseHandle registry.
manual: Signaling releases all registered waiters and remains signaled until reset. Already selected waiters retain their wake after a subsequent reset.
automatic: Signaling releases one pending waiter, or retains one signaled state if no waiter is pending. Repeated SetEvent does not accumulate a count when already signaled.
lifetime: Wait operations retain host object references. Same-process duplicates share state. Final handle close wakes pending waiters with invalid-handle failure rather than freeing live wait storage; concurrent final close is a defined port behavior, not a Windows compatibility guarantee.
limits: Named events, security attributes, interprocess inheritance and reduced-access duplication are explicit boundaries.
General multiple-object waits, alertable waits and PulseEvent remain unimplemented.
multiple_wait: Reached Miles wait-any pair only: index0 manual-reset event, index1 local recursive mutex. Atomic selection/acquisition under existing registry, event-before-mutex ordering, abandoned mutex status129, real native condition wakeups. Other combinations and wait-all explicitly stop.
